newsitem.title: NORWAY: Transocean wins two rig contracts.
newsitem.headline: Transocean wins two rig contracts.

text.p: Norwegian offshore company Transocean ASA said on Tuesday it had signed letters of intent for two of the company's modern deepwater drilling rigs amounting to $116.8 million.
The contracts cover the Transocean Rather and the Transocean Driller, the company said in a statement to the Oslo bourse.

The Transocean Rather, currently operating for Royal Dutch/Shell Group, is expected to be contracted to another operator for one firm year at around June 1998, or immediately upon conclusion of its current contract.
The letter-of-intent provides the operator with first right for refusal for a second year.
Transocean said estimated revenues over the one-year firm contract period would total $63.9 million. Copst of upgrading the rig for the project were around $5-6 million.

The Transocean Driller, currently operating for Elf in West Africa, is expected to be contracted to another operator for one firm year immediately after completion of its current project around July, 1997, Transocean said.
The operator also has the option for a second year.
Transocean said this deal was worth around $52.9 million for the firm 12-month period.
